reader.requirement: At --std 85, after a REWRITE of a relative file control transfers per §1985:VIII.1.3.5: on the invalid key condition (23) to the INVALID KEY imperative with no USE procedure, or, without INVALID KEY, to the USE procedure with NOT INVALID KEY ignored; on another exception (43, 44, 49) to the USE procedure with neither phrase run; on success to NOT INVALID KEY if written, else to the end of the statement; an explicit transfer (GO TO) in the imperative is honored. In random and dynamic access (sequential access writes no phrase, SR3).
reader.edition-search: grep -n 'Edition|Dialect|Version|IsActive' over KeyedIoEmitter.EmitRewrite, SequentialIoEmitter.EmitInvalid/EmitPhrasePair/EmitUseHook and KeyedIoBinder.BindRewrite: no edition term; the INVALID KEY branch is IoStatusClass.InvalidKey(st), the NOT branch IoStatusClass.Successful(st) gated by the USE hook, identical at every edition. (The phrase ORDER is gated at 85, which belongs to the format, recorded under GR11.)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness is DYNAMIC access with a RECORD VARYING file (23 with and without INVALID KEY, 44 to the USE procedure); RANDOM access, the FROM phrase, a GO TO out of the INVALID KEY imperative, the 49 not-open-I-O exception with both phrases written, and the sequential-access 43 are covered only by probe p5rwctl

probes.printed: K1 00 NOT-INVALID U=0 / K5 23 INVALID U=0 / USE-RR 23 / K6-NO-IK 23 NONE U=1 / K7 GOTO-M2 23 / K2-IK-ONLY 00 NONE U=1
probes.expected: RANDOM access: success with both phrases runs NOT INVALID KEY; a missing slot with INVALID KEY runs it and not the USE; without INVALID KEY the USE runs and NOT INVALID KEY is ignored; GO TO in INVALID KEY transfers to M-2; success with INVALID KEY only falls to the end

probes.printed: USE-RR 49 / K1-INPUT 49 NONE U=2 / R1 FROM-1 / R2 REC-2B / USE-RQ 43 / Q-NO-READ 43 / Q-AFTER-READ 00
probes.expected: an exception that is not invalid key (49, file open INPUT) runs the USE procedure and neither INVALID KEY nor NOT INVALID KEY (§1985:VIII.1.3.5 second list item 1); the FROM move rewrote record 1; sequential access without a prior READ is 43 to the USE, after a READ 00

citations.check: OK  §1985:VIII.4.6.4 GR10  (4.6.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR10

reader.notes: EmitRewrite stores the status, renders the USE hook with invalidKeyHandled set when INVALID KEY is written, then EmitPhrasePair branches INVALID KEY on the 2x class and NOT INVALID KEY on success. Every arm of §1985:VIII.1.3.5 was observed in random and dynamic access; nothing on the path depends on the edition.

refuter.evidence: Probe r10rw.cob (r10rw-001, --std 85), RANDOM access RECORD IS VARYING 5 TO 20 DEPENDING ON LN: REWRITE with LN=3 and with LN=21, both phrases written: status 44, the USE procedure runs, neither INVALID KEY nor NOT INVALID KEY (§1985:VIII.1.3.5 'not an invalid key' arm); REWRITE of missing RRN 5 with NOT INVALID KEY only: 23, the USE procedure runs, NOT INVALID KEY skipped; success with NOT INVALID KEY only: 'T4 NIK 00', USE not run; the record read back has LN=15. cite.py: OK  §1985:VIII.4.6.4 GR10  (4.6.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR10.
